cards.front: Recall a key point about Melody Writing
cards.back: Strong melodies have clear phrase structure — typically 4-bar or 8-bar phrases with a sense of question (antecedent) and answer (consequent).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Melody Writing
cards.back: Develop melodies through: sequence (repeating at a different pitch), inversion (turning upside down), augmentation (stretching), fragmentation (using part of the idea).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Melody Writing
cards.back: Match rhythm to genre: rock riffs use syncopation and repetition; Classical melodies use balanced phrasing; jazz melodies use swing and blue notes.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Melody Writing
cards.back: Staff notation requirements: you must submit a score in staff notation (up to 4 sharps/flats) — notation quality affects the AO2 mark for technical control.

cards.front: What should you know about music exam tips?
cards.back: Use balanced phrasing (4+4 bars). Apply development techniques (sequence, inversion). Match style to genre. Notate accurately. Annotate your decisions.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: A good melody just means something catchy that you like. Correct: Effective melody writing uses specific TECHNIQUES: balanced phrasing, motivic development (sequence, inversion, augmentation), appropriate rhythmic character for the genre, and coherent harmonic relationship. The exam assesses these technical skills, not whether the melody is catchy.
Compose an 8-bar melody in a specific style. Annotate your composition explaining the melodic techniques you used and how they serve the intended style.
AO1 — Knowledge: Show knowledge of Melody Writing using appropriate musical vocabulary (e.g. terminology for elements, devices, and contexts).

cards.front: Applying Melody Writing in Performance and Composition
cards.back: Understanding melody writing informs your performing (AO1) and composing (AO2) work. In performance, awareness of melody writing helps you make interpretive decisions that serve the music. In composition, melody writing provides the building blocks of your creative work — the choices you make about this element shape the identity and coherence of your piece.

cards.front: Exam Technique for Melody Writing Questions
cards.back: In the AQA GCSE Music listening exam, questions about melody writing typically ask you to: identify features by ear; describe how they are used; explain their effect; compare features between extracts. The key to success is precise terminology — never use vague language.
